title: Pick exactly one optimization dimension per WMBT

facts.note: Task text mentions authoring or revising a WMBT or its dimension.
Planning artifacts where WMBTs live; exact globs depend on repo topology.
Needs a structured diff observer that detects a WMBT entry being added or edited, including its dimension field.
Detector must parse WMBT entries and compare dimension against the six-value catalog; these findings activate the rule regardless of which part of the WMBT is being edited.
Whether the chosen dimension matches the user's intent can only be judged semantically.

fires: Planner writes a new WMBT for a wagon and must state what the user wants to optimize.
Planner edits an existing WMBT statement so that its optimization goal changes.
A WMBT statement names two metrics (e.g. faster and cheaper) and the planner must choose one.
Planner edits any part of a WMBT that currently has no dimension, several dimensions, or a dimension outside the catalog.
doesNotFire: Editing a WMBT's acceptance steps or wording without touching its dimension or optimization goal, when that WMBT already has exactly one catalog dimension.
Writing code, tests, or docs that are not WMBT planning artifacts.
Choosing the lens for a WMBT (covered by planner.wmbt.lens-selection).

given: A WMBT is being authored or revised from a user's intent
when: the planner states what the user wants to optimize
then: Select exactly one optimization dimension (the core metric the user wants to optimize) from: Time, Effort, Likelihood, Frequency, Quantity/Amount, Financial Value.
prefer: Match the user's intent to a dimension via its keywords; decompose into dimension/actor/action/object using the description and rationale.

Time = duration/speed/waiting/delay/rework (performer's most finite resource); Effort = physical or cognitive load (muscular force or concentration/learning/decision-making); Likelihood = probability of an outcome (predictability, control, success vs error).

Frequency = rate of occurrence (reduce repetitive/non-value-added tasks); Quantity/Amount = volume of a resource consumed or produced (optimize inputs/outputs); Financial Value = monetary impact (cost, revenue, opportunity cost).
Shape like: 'Time: minimize onboarding time', 'Likelihood: increase usable experiment results', 'Effort: reduce mental effort to find a bug'.
avoid: Assigning two or more dimensions to one WMBT; split the WMBT instead.
Using a dimension outside the six-value catalog.
why: One dimension names the core metric to optimize; statement templates and acceptance metrics derive from it, so mixing breaks that mapping.
evidence: Each WMBT has exactly one dimension, and it is one of the six catalog names.
Reviewer confirms the WMBT statement's optimization verb/object matches the chosen dimension's keywords and description.
verifier_detail: Dimension term structure: name -> {keywords, description}. Term id 'dimension', label 'Dimensions'.
Allowed names: Time, Effort, Likelihood, Frequency, Quantity/Amount, Financial Value. Flag zero or more-than-one dimension per WMBT, and any value outside this set.
